event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: STX’s 2022-08-05 10-K paints COVID-19 as a still-active, multi-dimensional threat.  The filing repeatedly confirms that the pandemic has ALREADY hurt the company—citing FY-2022 supply-chain bottlenecks, component shortages that throttled non-HDD sales, higher logistics and material costs, and variable customer demand.  It then layers forward-looking uncertainty, warning that further mutations, lockdowns or economic malaise could trigger manufacturing shutdowns, labour shortfalls, inventory imbalances, margin compression and even heightened cyber-exposure from remote work.  Only limited mitigating language appears (e.g., cost-control initiatives), and no quantified dollar figures are given, so risk remains high but not maximal.  Because the event is well within the 0-3-year ‘recent’ window, the Time Decay principle allows elevated scores (up to 10).  Sentences that describe concrete, already-realised impacts score toward the upper band (6-9), while purely contingent statements or those coupled with mitigation are tempered to mid-range (2-5).
